question: Can the Autel manual explain why every return-to-home attempt failed in the EVO Max 4N ASRS report?

intake.focus: Autel EVO Max 4N RTH failure ASRS
intake.reason: User asks whether the Autel EVO Max 4N manual explains why every return-to-home attempt failed in an ASRS report. Provide guidance from the Autel manual on RTH behavior and loss of control link, and note that ASRS reports are not verified findings. To determine applicability to a specific ASRS entry, we need the report's details (conditions, warnings, GPS loss, battery, interference) since the manual describes normal/failsafe RTH behavior and typical fault indicators rather than the exact ASRS case.

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance supports attempting to reestablish a control link and discontinuing flight if the link is not recoverable, and requires preflight control link loss procedures; example language frames loss-of-link scenarios. The Autel EVO Max 4N manual section is not found in the verified materials, so no usable evidence from the manual is available. Incident reports (unverified accounts) state loss of control shortly after takeoff and that the UAS was not located or recovered. Main gap: there is a conflict between FAA guidance to reestablish the control link and the unverified Autel report of sudden loss after takeoff, with no verified evidence of any RTH attempts or a manual explanation of why RTH would fail.
